label: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 13
knowledgePattern: Combine an exact truth count with implications between inequalities
solution:
Exactly one of IV and V is true, since they are complementary conditions on the same sum. Hence exactly one of I, II and III must be true.

If I were true, then x≤y+z≤|y|+|z|, making II true too. So I is false and x>y+z. Because |x|≥x, III must be true.

II must therefore be false: x>|y|+|z|. It follows that x+y+z>|y|+y+|z|+z≥0, so IV is true and V false.

The two true statements are III and IV. For consistency, x = 3, y = 1, z = 1 has exactly these truth values. Answer D.

hints.title: Find complementary statements
hints.body: Look for two listed inequalities that divide every real value of the same expression into disjoint cases.
hints.recap: Negating a strict inequality includes its equality boundary.
hints.pitfall: All statements refer to the same three real numbers.
hints.pause: Use their truth count to restrict the other statements.

recall.reminder: Negating a strict inequality includes its equality boundary.

hints.title: Follow implications between the remaining inequalities
hints.body: Compare y+z with |y|+|z|, and compare x with |x|. Use these comparisons with the required total number of truths.
hints.recap: When one statement forces another, their truth values cannot be chosen independently.
hints.pitfall: A single numerical example shows consistency, not that a pattern is forced.
hints.pause: Derive the necessary truth pattern rather than guessing values first.

recall.reminder: When one statement forces another, their truth values cannot be chosen independently.

hints.title: Return to the sign of the sum
hints.body: Use the inequalities you have forced to determine the sign of the original sum. Then supply one example checking every statement.
hints.recap: Absolute-value inequalities must be combined with their signs and endpoints intact.
hints.pitfall: Strictness matters when comparing the sum with zero.
hints.pause: Finish the classification and verify it is attainable.

recall.reminder: Absolute-value inequalities must be combined with their signs and endpoints intact.
